I am developing learning materials for students and others who want to understand statistics, research, and the use of data in practice. Elementary Statistics is the first course collection, but this section is intended to grow to include other courses, individual lectures, videos, and interactive resources.

## Courses and learning pathways

Courses bring related topics together in a sequence. Each course can have its own overview, lessons, examples, practice materials, and learning activities.

::: {.course-feature}

<span class="course-eyebrow">First course collection · In development</span>

### Elementary Statistics

This proposed course covers distributions, sampling, statistical inference, comparisons between groups, correlation, and regression. The overview includes an 18-week learning pathway and plans for laboratory activities.

The course page is a sample design, not a currently assigned class. Interactive lessons for Weeks 3 to 4 (describing distributions) and Week 6 (sampling distributions) are available. Other lessons remain in development.

[Explore Elementary Statistics](courses/elementary-statistics/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

:::

Additional courses can be added here as they are developed.

## Lectures, videos, and other learning resources

Not every topic needs a full course. I also plan to share shorter resources that can stand on their own, including recorded explanations, lecture-style presentations, worked examples, and interactive demonstrations.

This collection will be organized by topic so that visitors can find a specific explanation without following an entire course. There are no standalone lectures or videos available here yet; links will be added when the materials are ready.

## Planned Elementary Statistics activities

These are the first interactive resources in the development plan. The Weeks 3 to 4 and Week 6 lessons are available. Other lessons remain planned.

| Topic | Proposed weeks | Activity in development |
|---|---|---|
| [Describing distributions: center, spread, and outliers](courses/elementary-statistics/lessons/describing-distributions.qmd) | 3 to 4 | Interactive activity on mean, median, sample SD, and unusual values |
| [Sampling distributions and the central limit theorem](courses/elementary-statistics/lessons/sampling-distributions.qmd) | 6 | Interactive prototype: compare sample means and standard error at different sample sizes |
| Confidence intervals | 7 | Investigate coverage across repeated samples |
| Hypothesis tests and power | 8 | Explore sample size, variability, effect size, and statistical power |
| Correlation and regression | 14 to 15 | Examine association, prediction, outliers, and causal limitations |

Future activities will use browser-based tools where interaction improves learning. I will aim to include keyboard-accessible controls, clear explanations, and appropriate alternatives. Graded work and student records would remain in institutional course systems.

## Teaching approach

I want students to understand the reasoning behind statistical methods, rather than only learn which procedure to use.

I use questions from psychology, behavioral health, and everyday research to introduce concepts. I also favor worked examples, opportunities to practice, and discussion of the assumptions and limitations that matter when interpreting results.

## Research project guidance

Since 2016, I have provided periodic guidance to doctoral psychology interns at Didi Hirsch Mental Health Services as they work on their annual applied research or program evaluation project. My role is primarily to meet with the group, discuss their progress, and offer feedback on research and analysis questions as needed.

The contact is limited and focused on the project, generally consisting of several hours of meetings each month and occasional follow-up. This is one part of my research position, not a formal college teaching appointment.
